verdict_detail: On the C grid the H1 pair separates at n=48 already (100 % disjoint at 48/60/144; observed p95 intervals disjoint with 254 ms margin), so 144 is not what buys the separation; effective n at raw 144 is only 66, clearing the H1 floor of 60 by 10 %. For the 12-32 ms p50 gap seen in v3/v4 the plan is underpowered at every n tested up to 384. Recommendation: spend on runs (reps), not turns, because lag-1 0.4-0.66 makes extra turns within a run ~1/3 as informative as a new run; 3x48-turn runs of the pair (288 requests) tests replication of the 315 ms effect more cheaply than 4 arms x 144.
next_unit_hint: BUDGET-SCHEDULE should absorb: (1) no cell on disk exceeds 48 usable timings, so n=144 is an extrapolation everywhere; (2) the 315 ms p50 gap exists on rows-longrun-c only and is absent on v3/v4, so the budget's risk is replication, not p95 width; (3) if n>=60 effective is the real gate, only ~144 raw turns reach it. A follow-up unit could measure whether v3/v4 rows differ in arm definition (TURN-ROW-ATTRIBUTION) before spending 792 requests.
assumptions: Usable timing = kind=='turn' AND ttft_ms>0 AND timing_usable is not False; rows with timing_usable=False counted as dropped rather than silently included (worst case 14 of 192 in rows-longrun-c lease-reopen, 8 of 48 in v4 pointer-stable).
rows-longrun-2026-10-26.jsonl excluded (192 turn rows without ttft_ms); reconstructing ttft_s*1000 was refused as a different, unverified quantity.
Tool-grid distributions carry attribution_disputed and were never pooled with non-tools grids, so they inform neither the H1 pair nor the verdict.

Lag-1 is reported with its Fisher-z pooled value and effective n; the iid paired resampling in the power rows therefore overstates power for the high-lag arms, stated in the doc rather than modelled away.
